title: When the Deadline Falls
premise: Paloma Voss has spent nine years cleaning up deniable messes for the Meridian Office, an embassy that exists on no map and in no treaty. When a stranger named Elias Brand repays a favor she never performed — saving her life with evidence of a plot against her — he demands payment: help him extract Dr. Ilse Marchetti, a defector carrying proof that Meridian's director sold an asset network to a hostile service. As Paloma runs the extraction, she realizes Marchetti may be bait in a trap designed to flush out every fixer the Office ever burned, and that Brand's 'favor' was manufactured to bind her. In the end Paloma must choose between loyalty to the institution that made her and the truth that could destroy it: she burns her own legend, delivers the evidence to journalists instead of any government, and walks away alive but officially dead.
about_author: Ada Oyelaran is a former logistics consultant who spent years working near diplomatic corridors before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be forgettable, drawing on an obsession with paperwork, borders, and the lies nations tell themselves.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Paloma Voss's POV. A routine night in Vienna: she scrubs a diplomat's indiscretion from three databases, checks her go-bag by the door, and rehearses her cover story over cheap wine. The beat is controlled competence masking loneliness — we learn her rules, especially rule one: never owe anyone anything.

chapters.title: A Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Elias Brand appears at her safe flat with hospital records showing someone pulled her from a car crash in Riga two years ago — an event she has no memory of surviving. He says the debt is now due. Emotional beat: the floor tilts; her polished lie has a crack in it she never knew about.

chapters.title: Terms of Payment
chapters.summary: Brand's POV. He lays out the job: extract Dr. Ilse Marchetti from a psychiatric clinic outside Trieste before Friday, when she'll be transferred to Moscow. Brand claims Marchetti holds proof that Meridian's Director Calloway sold an asset network. Paloma refuses — then finds surveillance on her own building. Fear becomes leverage.

chapters.title: The Office That Isn't
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She reports the approach to her handler, Wren, inside Meridian's unmarked chancery. Wren is oddly calm, tells her to take the meeting and report everything. Paloma realizes she's being used as a probe — or set up. Beat: institutional trust curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Trieste Rain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Recon at the clinic under a cover identity as Marchetti's estranged niece. She confirms the transfer date but spots a second surveillance team — not Russian, not Meridian. Someone else wants Marchetti. Beat: the job just got crowded, and crowded means dangerous.

chapters.title: What Marchetti Knows
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. Inside the clinic, Ilse plays docile while mentally cataloguing her guards' rotations. Flashbacks reveal she was Calloway's analyst until she found the sell-out buried in wire-transfer metadata. Beat: quiet defiance; she's been waiting two years for someone competent to come.

chapters.title: Riga, Revisited
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She digs into her own erased past and finds the Riga crash was real — and that Brand pulled her out, meaning someone put her there. The trail points back to Meridian itself. Beat: vertigo; the debt may be a leash, and she's been wearing it for years.

chapters.title: Wren's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reports to Calloway that Paloma has taken the bait. We see the cold calculus: Marchetti is expendable, Paloma is a loose end, and Brand is the real target. Beat: dramatic irony — readers now know the extraction is theater staged for Paloma's benefit.

chapters.title: Two Teams, One Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wednesday night: the extraction begins. Paloma gets Marchetti out through the laundry dock seconds before the rival team hits the front entrance. A running gunfight in the rain; Brand covers their retreat and takes a graze. Beat: adrenaline and the first true alliance between Paloma and Brand.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe Silence
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. Hiding in a Slovenian farmhouse, Ilse tests Paloma, probing what she knows and who sent her. She reveals half the evidence — enough to prove the sale, not enough to survive without the rest, which is hidden where only a dead man can find it. Beat: wary mutual respect.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brand's POV. The rest of the evidence sits in a deposit box in Ljubljana under the name of Tomas Reiner — the asset Calloway sold, and the man whose death Brand witnessed. Brand confesses his motive isn't justice; it's guilt. Beat: Brand stops being a handler and becomes a person.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wren contacts Paloma directly: bring Marchetti in, and her Riga file disappears, her record stays clean. It's a genuine offer and they both know it. Paloma stalls. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme crystallizes — the institution offers survival priced in complicity.

chapters.title: Ljubljana, Closing Time
chapters.summary: Paloma and Brand's alternating POV. The bank retrieval goes wrong: Meridian's cleaners arrive early because Wren tracked Paloma's burner. They escape with the ledger but Brand is wounded badly. Beat: cost made physical; the plan is now bleeding.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. Ilse decrypts Reiner's records and finds something worse than the sale: a list of burned assets still active, including one name that makes Paloma go white — her own recruitment was engineered by the same operation. Beat: identity collapse; Paloma was built, not hired.

chapters.title: The Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She reconstructs the whole design: the Riga crash, the manufactured favor, the extraction window — all of it a machine to make her deliver Marchetti somewhere Meridian can bury them together. Beat: cold fury replacing fear; she decides to stop playing the piece and start playing the board.

chapters.title: Feeding the Machine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She feeds Wren a false location for a Thursday handover, buying time and misdirecting the cleaners. Marchetti objects — using herself as bait again. Paloma promises this time the trap faces the other way. Beat: resolve; the hunted begin hunting.

chapters.title: Thursday, Abandoned Quarry
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The handover site: Wren arrives expecting compliance, the rival team arrives expecting Meridian, and Paloma has wired the meet to record everything. The rival team turns out to be Russian intelligence recovering their purchased asset list. Chaos erupts. Beat: the trap springs on everyone at once.

chapters.title: Calloway Descends
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. With the quarry operation blown, the Director comes personally to Trieste to end it — revealing to Wren that Paloma was always meant to die in Riga, and that Wren's own name is on Reiner's ledger. Beat: the loyalist learns loyalty was always one-directional.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax begins: Calloway's cleaners corner them at the harbor warehouse. Brand, still bleeding, holds the door long enough for Paloma and Marchetti to reach the boat — and doesn't come out. Beat: sacrifice; the man who invented the debt pays it in full.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the water, pursued, Paloma makes her choice: instead of selling the ledger to any government, she transmits the entire archive — the sale, the burned assets, the Riga order — to journalists in four countries simultaneously. There is no taking it back. Beat: irrevocable commitment to truth over safety.

chapters.title: Paloma Voss, Deceased
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. One week later: headlines breaking, Meridian quietly dissolved into reorganization, Calloway gone before subpoenas land. Ilse testifies under protection. Paloma attends her own memorial service in disguise, watching strangers mourn a woman who never quite existed. Beat: elegiac freedom.

chapters.title: Rule One, Revised
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Epilogue in a small Portuguese coastal town: new name, no go-bag, a door she leaves unlocked for the first time in her life. A letter arrives containing only a Riga hospital bracelet — someone out there remembers. She smiles, files it away, and lives. Beat: hard-won peace with an open question.
